title: Do Not Trust the Benchmark: Limitations of General LLM Rankings and a Case for Task-Specific Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2609.23201v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Benchmark scores increasingly influence the development, marketing, and selection of large language models (LLMs). Yet an overall score is interpretable only in relation to the system tested, the questions included, and the conditions of evaluation. This perspective examines five connected limitations of general LLM rankings: differences between evaluated and publicly available systems; commercial incentives and dependencies in external evaluation; benchmark saturation, defective tests, and data contamination; models exploiting scoring procedures; and the limited relevance of general scores to users' tasks. Documented cases illustrate why these problems require different responses. I argue for evaluation procedures that disclose the tested configuration, validate questions and successful task completion, report performance alongside cost and execution time, and make the scope of generalization explicit. translated_title: 不要相信基准测试：通用大语言模型排名的局限性以及任务特定评估的案例
translated_abstract: 基准测试分数正日益影响着大语言模型（LLM）的开发、营销和选择。然而，一个总体分数只有在与被测试的系统、所包含的题目以及评估条件相关联时才具有可解释性。本观点文章考察了通用大语言模型排名的五个相互关联的局限性：被评估系统与公开可用系统之间的差异；外部评估中的商业激励与依赖关系；基准测试饱和、有缺陷的测试题以及数据污染；模型对评分程序的钻空子行为；以及通用分数与用户实际任务相关性有限。已记录的案例说明了为什么这些问题需要不同的应对措施。作者主张采用能够披露被测试配置、验证题目和成功任务完成情况、在报告性能的同时报告成本和执行时间、并明确泛化范围的评估程序。随后，作者讨论了 Isotanta（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文指出通用大语言模型基准排名存在五大局限性——评估系统与公开系统不一致、商业利益干扰、基准饱和与数据污染、模型钻评分规则空子、通用分数与用户任务脱节，并主张采用透明披露配置、经验证且同时报告成本与耗时的任务特定评估方法。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies five interconnected limitations of general LLM benchmark rankings and argues for transparent, validated, task-specific evaluation procedures that report performance alongside cost and execution time.
